Package leaflet: Information for the user
Fictamol 250 mg film-coated tablets

What is in this leaflet
1. What Fictamol is and what it is used for
2. What you need to know before you take Fictamol
3. How to take Fictamol
4. Possible side effects
5. How to store Fictamol
6. Contents of the pack and other information

1. What Fictamol is and what it is used for
Fictamol is a pain reliever. It is used to treat mild to moderate pain such as headache and toothache, and to reduce fever.

2. What you need to know before you take Fictamol
Do not take Fictamol if you are allergic to the active substance or to any of the other ingredients.
Talk to your pharmacist before taking Fictamol if you have liver problems or drink large amounts of alcohol.
Other medicines and Fictamol: tell your pharmacist if you are taking blood thinners such as warfarin.
Driving and using machines: Fictamol has no influence on the ability to drive.

3. How to take Fictamol
Adults and adolescents over 12 years: take 1 to 2 tablets with water every 6 hours as needed.
Do not take more than 8 tablets in 24 hours. Do not use for more than 3 days without talking to a doctor.

4. Possible side effects
Like all medicines, Fictamol can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them.
Uncommon side effects: nausea and stomach pain.
Rare side effects: skin rash and itching. Stop taking Fictamol and see a doctor if you get a skin rash.

5. How to store Fictamol
Store below 25 degrees Celsius in the original package to protect from moisture. Keep out of the sight and reach of children.

6. Contents of the pack and other information
Each tablet contains 250 mg of fictamol. The other ingredients are maize starch and magnesium stearate. Packs of 20 tablets.
